description_en: The domed temple dedicated to Bhagavatī (Mai) was constructed in the 20th century. The temple is situated on the western slope of Michāgāũ village.Enclosed within a walled area, the temple is accessible from the north. Adjacent to it, a roofed space is located in the southwest corner. Positioned at the center of the walled space, the temple stands independently. It was constructed using a combination of mud and stone masonry. With a square floor plan, the temple features a single door facing north. Prior to the entrance, two flag poles known asliṅgasare present. The temple's interior room reaches a height of nearly 100 cm. The roof consists of three stepped levels of stone slabs, with the final one shaped like a cross. Atop this structure sits a massive dome crafted from roughly cut stones of various sizes.This architectural style, inspired by the neo-classical monuments in Lucknow and subsequently introduced to the Kathmandu valley during the reign of Bhimsen Thapa (1775-1839), can be found in two locations within the Jumla district: the current temple in Michāgāũ and the Khalāchaur Śiva Mandira (JUM0303). Niels Gutschow studied similar dome temples in Far-West Nepal and observed that they were all built between the 1940s and 1980s (Gutschow 1992). Although the exact construction date of this temple is unknown, it is reasonable to suggest that it was built during the latter half of the 20th century.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: REFERENCES Gutschow, Niels, 1992, “The need to build a temple. Observations on building traditions in change in Western Nepal”, in Aspects of Nepalese Traditions , Bernhard Kolver (ed.). Stuttgart: Franz Steiner Verlag, pp. 97-121.
